comparator.name: University College Venlo
comparator.sourceNotes: Articles 3.6, 3.8 and 3.9 and Appendix I of the 2026–27 regulations govern this example. It uses a single formal concentration and illustrates 15 EC of general education and 75 EC of concentration courses. The three food-system pillars are thematic directions. The regulations specify social-science and life-science concentration arrangements, with different general education rules for interdisciplinary study. The four introductory skills trainings and two core projects total 20 EC. Appendix I and the catalogue additionally list the advanced 2.5 EC Portfolio as core, although Article 3.8 summarises the combined core skills and project allocation as 20 EC. This example follows the itemised requirements, listing Portfolio separately in the final year. With 20 EC of core courses, 20 EC of introductory core skills and projects, 2.5 EC Portfolio, 15 EC general education, 75 EC concentration courses, 12.5 EC concentration skills, 15 EC concentration projects and 20 EC Capstone, the total is 180 EC.
components: Biological Foundations of Nutrition and Health
Knowledge, Evidence and Decision-Making under Uncertainty
Food in Transition: An Interdisciplinary Systems Perspective
This is the last part of a three-period group research project. Students analyse their data, write an article and present a poster.
Designing Research: Quantitative and Qualitative Approaches
This 2.5 EC pass/fail module is listed in the fifth semester. It records curriculum choices and personal and professional development.
The example uses 15 EC outside a single concentration, including humanities and the alternate concentration. Interdisciplinary curricula instead require 10 EC of humanities.
The example uses 75 EC of concentration courses. The concentration requires at least 20 EC of advanced coursework and allows at most 20 EC of introductory coursework.
Choose five intermediate or advanced skills trainings.
Choose three concentration projects, including at least one advanced project.
Students need at least 140 EC before beginning the required 20 EC final project.

core: Academic core: the four core courses on the biology of nutrition and health, behaviour and decision-making, knowledge, evidence and decision-making under uncertainty (philosophy of science), and global sustainability challenges, with the Food in Transition systems project

Research methods, statistics and applied research training: designing quantitative and qualitative research, the Applied Researcher project sequence with statistical analysis, data visualisation, laboratory skills and science communication
Sustainable food systems and their environmental dimension: sustainable agriculture and food production, the environmental impact of food and global sustainability challenges
Cross-pillar integration: building a curriculum across the behaviour, health and responsible-innovation pillars to connect disciplines in the food system
Advanced concentration depth: at least 20 EC of advanced courses over no fewer than three courses, an advanced project and the 20-EC Capstone
adjacent: Health pillar: how nutrition affects the body and society, covering nutrition, metabolism, physiology, disease mechanisms, pharmacology and public health
Behaviour pillar: why people do what they do around food, covering consumer behaviour, decision-making, the psychology of eating, behaviour change and sensory perception
Responsible-innovation pillar: how knowledge becomes real change, covering entrepreneurship, product innovation, markets and economics, governance, regulation and policy
questions: Why do people eat unhealthily even when they know better, and how can food choices and health behaviour be changed?
How can sustainable food innovations reach the market and how can regulation steer food systems towards health and sustainability?
How do food production and consumption affect the environment and climate, and what must be done about it?

trace: introduces how cells, molecules and organ systems interact, including how cells take in energy and nutrients and convert them into usable forms; it directly implements the biological-foundations strand of the academic core, although it contains no nutrition-specific content
Examines climate drivers, impacts on agriculture and health, mitigation and adaptation. It supplies climate context for food systems.
teaches epidemiology and public health, including lifestyle-related disease and the critical evaluation of evidence; it directly implements the public-health evidence strand of the health pillar
Develops a consumer product through needs research, prototyping and consideration of production. The design process provides relevant foundations for responsible innovation.

teaches research design, operationalization, sampling, experiments and surveys together with descriptive and inferential statistics and ANOVA; it directly implements the research-design and statistics training of the methods strand
develops data visualization, cleaning and manipulation with datasets from several disciplines; it directly implements the data-visualisation and data-handling skills of the methods strand
covers social cognition, attitudes, groups and social influence on behaviour; it directly implements the psychological foundation of the behaviour pillar
Uses supply, demand, consumer choice and production costs to explain markets. These tools can be applied to food markets.

has teams build a start-up concept from ideation to pitch with design thinking, market validation and business planning; it makes a specific complementary contribution to bringing sustainable food technologies to market as the entrepreneurship foundation of the responsible-innovation pillar

evaluates the environmental, social and health consequences of products and processes across their whole life cycle with life-cycle assessment and circular-economy strategies; it directly implements the whole-chain, systems perspective on the environmental impact of food and products

covers the biochemistry of proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids, metabolic pathways and energy metabolism; it directly implements the macronutrient biochemistry and metabolism that underlie nutrition

analyses consumer decision-making under uncertainty, cognitive limitations, market structures, externalities and the role of government; it directly implements decision-making and market analysis at intermediate level

examines market failure, externalities, public goods, taxation and the economic effects of public policy; it directly implements the economics of public intervention behind food policy and regulation, without food-specific content

studies the environmental harm of current farming, sustainable livestock farming, integrated pest management and sustainable supply chains; it directly implements sustainable agriculture and food production and is the one UCR course on food production

trains the evaluation of evidence, the demarcation of science from pseudoscience and the handling of misinformation; it directly implements the evidence-and-knowledge strand of the core, although it is not a philosophy-of-science course

examines institutional, political and cultural forces on global business, cross-border governance, corporate responsibility and global trade; it makes a specific complementary contribution to how products travel through global chains and are governed, without food-specific content

covers basic cell processes, homeostasis, the organ systems including digestion, metabolism, growth and ageing; it directly implements the human-body, homeostasis and metabolism strand of the biological core
Studies persuasion, message framing and audience responses. These methods help analyse how health and sustainability information shapes behaviour.

integrates psychology into economics to study how biases, heuristics and framing shape decisions, with behavioural experiments; it directly implements the behaviour-and-decision-making strand of the core
unpacks consumer behaviour and engagement, marketing strategy and responsible customer trust; it directly implements consumer behaviour as it bears on marketing sustainable products
Uses stakeholder and policy analysis to evaluate interventions in sustainability transitions. This provides governance methods applicable to food systems.
Examines biodiversity loss, habitat change and conservation responses, with a local threatened-species project. It gives ecological context for changes in land use.

introduces why people behave as they do, nature and nurture and brain-behaviour relations as the gateway to the health and psychology courses; it serves as the formal prerequisite of the neuroscience and psychology courses of this programme and makes a specific complementary contribution to the behavioural side of health

examines the structure of the human body in relation to function using imaging, surface anatomy and dissection materials; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the organ-system knowledge on which nutrition and health depend
Examines neural mechanisms of sensory processing and goal-directed action. This provides foundations for studying perception and behaviour.

teaches multivariate statistics including regression, factor analysis and ANOVA/ANCOVA for research on human health and behaviour; it directly implements intermediate statistical methods for health research

takes a close look at the cell biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes and its applications in medicine, industry and agriculture; it directly implements the molecular-biology strand of the health pillar
Uses laboratory practice in blood analysis, aseptic technique, bacterial identification and related biological measurements. These techniques support empirical life-science work.

presents how defects in structure and function cause disease across six organ systems including the digestive tract and endocrine glands; it directly implements the disease-mechanism strand of the health pillar at advanced level
covers the principles of pharmacology, drug action, therapeutic use and toxicity; it directly implements the pharmacology and toxicology strand of the health pillar at advanced level

covers general and molecular pathology and genetics, including cell injury, inflammation and immunity; it makes a specific complementary contribution to understanding disease mechanisms at advanced level
examines the bio-psycho-social interplay behind health and illness, health-psychology theory and interventions; it directly implements the behavioural drivers of health at advanced level

explains immune recognition, host-pathogen interactions, inflammation and immunopathology; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the host-defence side of health and disease at advanced level
Teaches systematic literature searching, study selection, risk of bias and quantitative evidence synthesis. This supports evaluating health and behaviour research.

explores human development across the lifespan, including cognitive and social development and ageing; it makes a specific complementary contribution to life-course health, the territory of the UCV course on drivers of health over the life cycle

Research teams develop a question, collect qualitative evidence using techniques such as interviews or observation, code and interpret material, and report findings and limitations. This supports social inquiry into choices and practices across food systems.

provides a sociological toolkit for analysing everyday interactions, social institutions and global phenomena; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social and institutional processes shaping behaviour

analyses how the climate crisis is communicated and contested across texts, media and protest and culminates in a debate project; it makes a specific complementary contribution to how messages about sustainability shape and fail to shape behaviour

deepens cognitive neuroscience of memory, emotion, social cognition, attention and decision making and trains experimental design; it directly implements the cognitive basis of decision-making at advanced level
trains how to gather customer opinions and test business ideas through market research; it directly implements consumer-research methods and consumer insight at advanced level

candidates.label: Health pillar: nutrition, human biology and public health
Behaviour pillar: food choice, consumer behaviour and decision-making
Responsible innovation pillar: sustainable food innovation, markets and entrepreneurship
Food policy and regulation for health and sustainability

selection.assessment: Three distinct plans address the shared food-system themes and the health and behaviour pillars. Farming and life-cycle analysis connect production with environmental effects. Biology, population health and clinical research methods support the health direction, while psychology, economic decisions and consumer research support the behaviour direction. Responsible innovation and regulation have support in the closest plan and remain separate candidate emphases beyond the three-option limit. Specialist nutrition, food technology, safety and sensory science remain limitations.

blocks: Academic core, evidence and research training
Both develop academic inquiry, including evaluating sources and framing research questions. UCR also covers personal development and community engagement.
Both develop research design and measurement. UCR also teaches descriptive and inferential statistics in this course.
Both examine evidence and the reliability of claims. UCR focuses on misinformation and misleading reasoning, while Venlo examines how knowledge and evidence inform decisions under uncertainty.
Both develop team research and the reporting of findings. UCR focuses on qualitative research. Venlo completes a linked research sequence with data analysis in R, an article and a poster.
Both develop data analysis skills. Venlo collects and analyses data within an ongoing group project, while UCR studies experimental design and multivariate statistics.
Venlo begins a supervised research project with a group proposal. UCR develops research planning within methods courses.
Venlo’s final-year Portfolio follows development across the degree. UCR’s Personal & Professional Development course is taken in Year 1.
Both examine how the body functions, including digestion and metabolism. Venlo gives greater attention to nutrition and macronutrients.
Both examine judgement, incentives and biases. Venlo applies the material to questions of food choice, health and sustainability.
Sustainability, food production and global challenges
Both examine sustainability challenges and connections between society and environmental change. UCR focuses on climate drivers, impacts and responses.
Both take a whole-system view of environmental effects. UCR uses life-cycle assessment, while Venlo models interactions within food systems.
Open concentration, general education and Capstone
The example uses 15 EC outside a single concentration, including humanities and the alternate concentration. Interdisciplinary curricula instead require 10 EC of humanities.
The example uses 75 EC of concentration courses. The concentration requires at least 20 EC of advanced coursework and allows at most 20 EC of introductory coursework.
Choose five intermediate or advanced skills trainings.
Choose three concentration projects, including at least one advanced project.
Venlo requires a 20 EC Capstone after at least 140 EC. UCR’s 15 EC optional independent research is shown separately from the scheduled courses.

notes.text: Venlo brings together behaviour, health and responsible innovation around food systems. The UCR plans offer related perspectives through farming and sustainability, human biology and public health, or psychology and consumer research.

Venlo offers specialist courses in nutrition, food processing and safety, sensory science and food product development. The UCR plans cover related topics through broader courses. Venlo also requires a 20 EC Capstone.

audience.programmeDescription: University College Venlo is an English-taught liberal arts and sciences bachelor focused on sustainable food systems. It examines how food is produced, how people make choices and how food affects health and the environment.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR plans illustrate three related directions. The Venlo example follows the named modules in the regulations and catalogue. It includes the 2.5 EC final-year Portfolio separately from the 20 EC of introductory skills and projects, since the regulations give different totals in their summary and module list.
